text:
Mason Marchment is on his sixth NHL team, the undrafted winger who has made a career out of being useful wherever he lands. In San Jose that means 16:37 a night, six goals and 12 points in 25 games, and a shootout winner against Utah on Nov. 14.

The numbers around him are rough. The Sharks get only 41% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice, and his scoring rate sits a touch below his own talent range. Some of that is bad luck: San Jose has scored about four fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there. His own shooting looks normal, 13% on chances that deserve about what he has.

Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 93rd among 401 forwards, driven by even-strength offense, with good defensive marks too. One thing to watch: Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest noted the second power-play unit has moved Marchment to the net front, with Michael Misa on the flank. A 6'5" body in front is an easy fit.
headline: Mason Marchment, sixth team, new spot in front
